title: P2/P5 — Predictable Web draft capacity and bounded research-context recovery
body:
The completed research handoff in #1366 exposed avoidable Web editing and recovery burden: four attempted additions exceeded the selected-source budget. The shortest added 211 text characters but 1,777 canonical bytes, taking the selection to 12,177 bytes. The successful revision retained 11,947 of 12,000 bytes. Recovery took about 27 minutes 32 seconds of agent wall time, not measured human labor. Historical failed payloads were reconstructed, not captured wire requests. The actual refusal was `selected_source_context_budget_exceeded` (HTTP 422), not the relation or request-body limit.

Implement a bounded P2/P5 follow-up (owners #1212 / #1215; coordination #1209):

- Show current-draft capacity before persistence, using the actual admission normalization and canonical byte accounting. Distinguish note count, per-note text, source bytes, and other relevant constraints.
- Keep invalid and over-budget drafts editable. Explain how to revise whole notes and required context while preserving attribution and earlier revisions. Inspection must neither save nor silently rewrite content, and final save/currentness checks remain authoritative.
- Measure text versus metadata cost and test a plausible update to a near-full work. Decide whether feedback plus existing revision editing is sufficient or a modest, compatible capacity change is justified; native 32,000-byte admission is a separate contract.
- Cover Unicode, boundaries, metadata, edits/dependencies, stale feedback, replay, failed saves, reopen and complete export with prior lineage preserved. Use synthetic fixtures and report editing steps and unsuccessful attempts without claiming general usability or time savings.

Scope: current-source diagnosis, bounded implementation, focused checks and planner-required exact-head verification, and one Draft PR. Preserve #1366’s completed disposition and private evidence; no private exports, identifiers or artifact contents in commits or this issue. No deployment, cloud/configuration/credential changes, unrelated saved work, automatic summarization, schema/storage redesign or artifact hosting. Deployment and hosted acceptance require separate review.

## Reviewed implementation closeout — 2026-09-30

Completed through user-merged PR #1370. The reviewed head was `1939f66145647134e594579c79153da49505f951`. Fresh GitHub reads confirm merge/current main `7d4320a4c6ebd08f2f8b4e530f5150d972a58ec1`, tree `d64a66979d7d51ebe4603354dc57e46624987c4d`, identical to the reviewed head's tree. No new merge-head verification run is claimed.

Review covered all 14 changed files, shared admission accounting, response invalidation, retained editability and the synthetic save/reopen/export path. No blocking source issue was found. Storage limits and saved formats remain unchanged. The constructed near-full update reached 10,954/12,000 source bytes after two recovery edits and zero unsuccessful UI saves, with original history and required lineage retained; known redundant fixture detail limits generalization.

The PR records focused checks, one 16/16 Full Local Canonical PASS, valid receipt and completed cleanup for the exact reviewed head. These execution results are accepted as the submitted local report; the reviewer did not independently revalidate the raw Mac-local receipt or rerun Canonical. Development failures and evidence retain their recorded status.

This closes the bounded implementation and review scope. Deployment and hosted acceptance remain separate and unperformed by this closeout. #1366's completed research disposition and original artifacts remain intact. Broader capacity adequacy and general usability remain follow-up observations.
